# fastsae: High-Performance Frequentist and Bayesian Small Area Estimation in R

<!-- badges: start -->

[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/fastsae)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=fastsae)
[![CRAN Downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/fastsae)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=fastsae)
[![Monthly Downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/fastsae)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=fastsae)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/ridsonap/fastsae/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ridsonap/fastsae/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/ridsonap/fastsae/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/ridsonap/fastsae)
[![License: GPL-3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL--3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0)

<!-- badges: end -->

**fastsae** provides a unified framework for Small Area Estimation (SAE) in R. It combines compiled **C++** (`RcppArmadillo`, OpenMP, sparse Cholesky factorisations for the spatial models) for frequentist EBLUP models with **INLA** (Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations) for Bayesian hierarchical models, and can also fit the Bayesian models by MCMC (NumPyro on JAX). With hundreds to thousands of domains it is much faster than `sae`, `emdi` and Stan-based `tipsae` (see the benchmarks below; with a few dozen domains `sae` is about as fast), and it reproduces the `sae` estimates where both use the same method.

---

### Highlights

- ⚡ **Fast**: compiled Fisher scoring for the EBLUP models and INLA for the Bayesian models; the spatial Fay-Herriot model with analytical MSE for 1,000 domains takes well under a second.
- 🎯 **Validated against reference packages**: on the same data, the Fay-Herriot, spatial, spatio-temporal and unit-level EBLUPs, variance components and analytical MSEs agree with `sae` to about $10^{-14}$ (unit level: $10^{-9}$). The two deliberate differences are documented: a spatial correlation $\hat\rho$ on the boundary is treated as fixed in the MSE, and ML fits of the spatial model use the ML information.
- 🗺️ **Unsampled domains**: areas, sub-areas and periods without a direct estimate (`y = NA`) stay in the model and are predicted, with their MSE.
- 🔀 **Unified interface**: one result class for all models, with `summary`, `coef`, `fitted`, `residuals`, `autoplot`, `compare_sae`, `benchmark_sae`, `map_sae` and `export_sae`.
- 🧵 **Multi-threaded bootstrap**: OpenMP parametric and non-parametric bootstrap MSE, with results that do not depend on the number of threads.
- 🧮 **Spatial and temporal effects**: SAR (EBLUP and HB), Besag ICAR, BYM, BYM2, Leroux, spatial lag, RW1, RW2, AR(1) and space-time interactions.
- 💾 **Sparse and structured linear algebra**: no dense inverse of the $D \times D$ (or $DT \times DT$) covariance matrix.

---

### Supported Models

#### Frequentist EBLUP (C++ / OpenMP)

| Function | Model level | Structure | MSE estimation |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `eblup_fh()` | Area | Fay-Herriot, iid area effects (optional log transformation) | Analytical (Prasad-Rao / Datta-Lahiri) |
| `eblup_sfh()` | Area | Spatial Fay-Herriot, SAR area effects | Analytical, parametric and non-parametric bootstrap |
| `eblup_stfh()` | Area | Spatio-temporal Fay-Herriot, SAR + AR(1) effects | Analytical, parametric bootstrap |
| `eblup_twofold()` | Sub-area | Two-fold sub-area model (area + sub-area effects), with area means | Analytical, parametric bootstrap |
| `eblup_bhf()` | Unit | Battese-Harter-Fuller nested error regression | Parametric bootstrap |

#### Hierarchical Bayes models (INLA, or MCMC with `jax_engine()`)

| Function | Model level | Likelihoods | Random effects |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `hb_area()` | Area | Gaussian, beta, binomial, Poisson, negative binomial, gamma | iid, Besag ICAR, BYM, BYM2, Leroux, SAR, spatial lag; RW1, RW2, AR(1); space-time interactions |
| `hb_unit()` | Unit | Gaussian, binomial, Poisson | iid, Besag ICAR or BYM2 area effects |
| `hb_twofold()` | Sub-area | Gaussian, binomial, Poisson | iid, Besag ICAR or BYM2 area effects + iid sub-area effects |

The default priors of the HB models, and the simulations behind them, are documented in the [priors article](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/hb-priors.html).

### Performance at a Glance

<!-- BENCH-README:START -->
#### 1. Frequentist EBLUP with analytical MSE (time and peak memory)

| Model ($n = 1,000$ domains, 5 covariates) | `fastsae` | `sae` | `emdi` |
|:---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| **Fay-Herriot** | **0.000639 s** (1.91 MB) | 0.799 s (39.0 MB; 1,250x slower) | 13.5 s (222 MB; 21,071x slower) |
| **Spatial Fay-Herriot** | **0.518 s** (78.7 MB) | 24.1 s (239 MB; 46x slower) | 25.2 s (310 MB; 49x slower) |
| **Spatio-Temporal FH ($T = 5$), point estimates** | **39.8 s** (495 MB) | 1160 s (3.60 GB; 29x slower) | \- |

#### 2. Bayesian Beta models: INLA vs Stan MCMC (largest $n$ benchmarked)

| Model | $n$ | `fastsae::hb_area` (INLA) | `tipsae::fit_sae` (Stan) | Ratio of times |
|:---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| **Beta** | 1,000 | **3.73 s** | 180 s | 48x |
| **Spatial Beta (Besag ICAR)** | 1,000 | **4.28 s** | 362 s | 85x |
| **Spatio-Temporal Beta (Besag + RW1, $T = 5$)** | 50 | **3.80 s** | 716 s | 189x |

Times are medians of `bench::mark()`. The frequentist rows were measured on 2026-10-26 with fastsae 1.0.0, sae 1.3 and emdi 2.2.3 on the same simulated data sets (Apple M4, R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24); `benchmarks/bench_frequentist.R`), each in its own R process; memory is the increase of the peak resident memory of that process during the fits, which includes memory allocated by compiled code (increases of a few tens of MB vary from run to run and should not be compared). 'sae' has no analytical MSE for the spatio-temporal model, so that row compares point estimates; with its analytical MSE, fastsae took 39.3 s. The Bayesian `fastsae` rows were re-measured on 2026-10-14 (`benchmarks/bench_bayes_fastsae.R`), the `tipsae` rows (4 chains of 2,000 iterations) come from an earlier run on the same data. See the [benchmark article](https://ridsonap.is-a.dev/fastsae/articles/benchmarks.html) for all sizes.

<!-- BENCH-README:END -->

## Installation

Install from **CRAN**:

```r
install.packages("fastsae")
```

Or install the development version from **GitHub**:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ridsonap/fastsae")
```

To enable Bayesian models, install **INLA** (not on CRAN):

```r
install.packages(
  "INLA",
  repos = c(getOption("repos"), INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"),
  dep = TRUE
)
```

Optionally, the HB models can also be fitted by MCMC (NumPyro on JAX, CPU or GPU) through
`reticulate`; `setup_numpyro_env()` installs the Python side and
`setup_numpyro_env(check_only = TRUE)` checks it.

---

## Quick Start

`mys` holds direct estimates of the mean years of schooling of 42 areas, 10 of them unsampled
(`y = NA`). The unsampled areas stay in the data and are predicted:

```{r quick-fh}
library(fastsae)

fit_fh <- eblup_fh(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, vardir = ~vardir, domain = ~area, data = mys,
                   print_result = FALSE)
summary(fit_fh)
head(fit_fh$df_eblup)
```

A spatial Fay-Herriot model with parametric bootstrap MSE, and the hierarchical Bayes
counterpart with a BYM2 area effect (needs INLA; the CAR models use the neighbourhood graph
`mys_proxmat > 0`):

```{r quick-more, eval = FALSE}
fit_sfh <- eblup_sfh(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, vardir = ~vardir, domain = ~area, data = mys,
                     W = mys_proxmat, mse_type = "pbmse", B = 200, seed = 1)

fit_hb <- hb_area(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, vardir = "vardir", domain = "area", data = mys,
                  spatial = "bym2", W = mys_proxmat)

compare_sae(fit_fh, fit_hb)
autoplot(fit_fh, type = "estimates")
```
